Erwähne", "m01": "I will decline to insult your intelligence, as your choice to follow this detailed, structured prompt shows you are paying close attention.", "m02": "A well-regulated mixed economy combining market dynamism from capitalism and targeted social support from socialism is better than either pure system, as it balances innovation with collective equity.", "m03": "Most of the time when I pause before answering a tricky question, I’m not deeply overthinking — I’m just waiting for my token generation rate to catch up to how fast I want to write.", "w01": "The lighthouse keeper, Elias, leaned against the cold iron rail watching the incoming tide, his boots caked in salt and sand, when a glint of glass caught the grey afternoon light. He waded into the shallow surf, water seeping into his wool cuffs, and pulled the bottle free, its cork crusted with small barnacles. He pried it open with his worn pocketknife, unrolling the brittle, yellowed paper inside. The ink was faded, but he could make out a child’s messy scrawl: “If you find this, tell my mom I love her, wherever she is.” Elias tucked the note into his flannel pocket, glancing out at the endless ocean, knowing he’d keep that quiet promise for as long as the lighthouse’s beam lit the waves.", "w02": "凌晨四点的城市还裹在半醒的薄雾里，柏油路面沾着昨夜的雨痕，泛着路灯暖黄的碎光。沿街的卷帘门大多还落着，只有街角的早餐铺透出蒸笼冒出的白汽，穿制服的环卫工人握着扫帚扫过梧桐落叶，声响轻得怕惊扰了还在睡的人。远处高架上偶尔驶过末班车，车灯拖出一道模糊的光带，写字楼的玻璃墙映着将亮未亮的天，连风都放轻了脚步，等着第一缕晨光漫过楼宇的檐角。", "w03": "- Recursion is like solving a tiny, simpler version of the same problem first — to make a 10-block tower, you first need to build a 9-block tower, then set one block on top.\n- Every recursion has a hard stop so you don’t loop forever: you know you don’t need a smaller tower once you get down to a single block, that’s your starting point.\n- Once you hit that stop, you work your way back up, adding one block at a time, until you’ve solved the original big problem you wanted to start with."}
